answer: A practical sybil defense ties each identity to a scarce, verifiable resource commitment, such as a hardware-bound key plus a modest stake. Ferrous-strong binding means one device backs one identity, so cloning requires buying new hardware for every fake. A saffron flag marks accounts whose stake arrived minutes before their first job, letting clients discount fresh, unproven actors. Quartz-like transparency completes the picture: stakes, jobs and payments sit on a public ledger, so a hundred identities mean a hundred stakes and a hundred visible trails.
